subject: Acme streaming SLOs: measurement plan, prompt ownership, and harness handoff
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Acme streaming SLOs: measurement plan, prompt ownership, and harness handoff

Hi Tara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan for the SLO qualification work on the checkout streaming flow.

Summary of what we heard from Acme on the call:
- Primary goal: provide a streaming assistant in checkout that keeps perceived latency low while allowing progressive enrichment of product suggestions.
- Traffic profile: ~6k checkout sessions/day at peak, median session length 18 tokens produced, bursty spikes around promotions (targeting 2x baseline for safety).
- Success criteria (customer stated): first-byte perceived latency <= 200 ms at p95, steady-state per-token latency <= 30 ms p95, and ability to sustain 120 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation.

Redwood proposed SLO hypotheses (for qualification):
1) P95 first-byte server-side latency <= 200 ms for streaming endpoints under normal network conditions (us-west region).
2) Steady-state per-token p95 <= 30 ms measured from server send to network egress.
3) Throughput: sustain 120 concurrent streaming sessions (defined below) with end-to-end 95th latency below targets.
4) Degradation policy: at >150 concurrent sessions, fallback to 1) reduced sampling rate or 2) lower quantized model with <10% quality delta measured by provided prompt bundle.

Definitions to use during benchmarking (we'll formalize these in the attached measurement-definitions.md):
- "first_byte_latency": time from request arrival at Redwood front proxy to first chunk emitted to client.
- "steady_token_latency": rolling p95 of per-token emission time once streaming has started (exclude first N tokens; see harness config).
- "concurrent_streaming_session": single checkout session that receives a streaming response; counted while connection remains open.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Acme: confirm the traffic shape (burst multiplier and sample session traces) and mark which prompts we should prioritize from your side. (Tara, you said you'd share sample traces.)
2) Redwood (Marissa): we will deliver an initial harness config + prompt bundle and a reproducibility checklist by EOD today.
3) Schedule a 45-minute handoff with Acme eng and Redwood perf to run through the harness and mapping of metrics to your APM dashboards. Proposed slot: Thu 5/21 10:00-10:45 PT.

Attachments included: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts from the discovery call), harness-config-20260519.yaml (initial harness settings), measurement-definitions.md (draft measurement glossary).

If this aligns, I'll mark the HubSpot deal with these next steps and get the calendar invite out.

Thanks — Grace
--
Grace O'Connor

From: Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Acme streaming SLOs: measurement plan, prompt ownership, and harness handoff

Grace — thank you for the clear recap. That matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from Acme eng:
- Peak day sessions may be closer to 8k in heavy promo windows; please size the burst at 3x baseline for the stress runs.
- For perceived latency we care most about time to first meaningful token (not just a keepalive chunk). Please include a measurement that captures "first_meaningful_token" in addition to first_byte.

I'll upload two sample session traces and our synthetic traffic generator config to the shared Drive folder by EOD. We can prioritize prompt IDs 1-25 in the prompt set for the first pass.

Confirming Thu 5/21 10:00 PT for the handoff; acme-eng will join.

Thanks — Tara
Tara Liu

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Liu <tara.liu@acme-retail.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme streaming SLOs: measurement plan, prompt ownership, and harness handoff

Adding the perf/harness perspective and the artifacts we'll hand over. Attached are: harness-config-20260519.yaml and measurement-definitions.md. I also exported a trimmed prompt bundle as acme_prompt_set_v1.csv per Grace's ask.

Key measurement and reproducibility requirements (summary):
- Model pinning: tests must include exact model id (e.g., rw-infer/open-stream-v1@20260501) and quantization profile. No fuzzy "latest" tags for reproducibility.
- Environment spec: GPU type (A100-40GB), CUDA/cuDNN versions, batch sizes, and contiguous KV cache reset behavior. We'll include a docker-compose snippet in the harness config.
- Determinism: for quality comparisons use deterministic sampling (top-k deterministic seeds) for the first baseline runs. For production-like sampling we will run N stochastic seeds and report mean/std of quality metrics.
- Prompt handling: prompts in acme_prompt_set_v1.csv include explicit stop tokens and role tags; we will run runs both as single-turn and multi-turn to capture prefix caching effects.
- Metrics we will output from the harness: first_byte_latency, first_meaningful_token_latency, steady_token_p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, max_concurrent_sessions, and per-prompt quality scores (BLEU-ish and semantic-similarity scores we discussed).
- Warmup and prefill: harness will do a 120-second warmup at 10% load, then ramp to target. We'll log warmup performance and exclude warmup from steady-state stats unless requested.

Handover artifacts attached:
- harness-config-20260519.yaml: contains endpoint targets, load profile, concurrency plan, seed list, sampling mode, and export targets.
- measurement-definitions.md: canonical definitions for every metric we will report (helps map to your APM).
- acme_prompt_set_v1.csv: 120 sample prompts (we'll prioritize 25 as Tara requested).

One operational ask: please confirm whether Acme wants metrics exported from Redwood's console (we can push to your DataDog account) or whether you prefer raw CSV outputs for ingestion.

I will also include a short reproducibility checklist in the agenda for Thu's handoff.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is great. Confirming Redwood will: 1) run the initial qualification harness using the attached config and prompt bundle, 2) produce a reproducibility report that includes exact model pins, env specs, and raw harness outputs, and 3) propose fallback thresholds after the first run.

I've scheduled the 45-minute handoff for Thu 5/21 10:00-10:45 PT and shared a calendar invite with acme-eng. Agenda will be: 1) quick alignment on definitions (10m), 2) harness walkthrough (20m), 3) mapping metrics to Acme dashboards and next steps (15m).

Tara — for the export option, we'll plan to both push metrics to your DataDog integration and attach CSV exports to the reproducibility bundle unless you tell us to do otherwise.
